doc_summary: The paper operationalizes 'belief depth' for implanted facts via generality, robustness to scrutiny, and internal-representation similarity, finding synthetic document finetuning (SDF) implants deep beliefs while prompting and mechanistic editing do not. It also shows that document realism matters less than consistency/diversity and that models can know documents are synthetic yet still update on them.

items.claim: Prefers multi-pronged evidence of genuine belief (downstream use, robustness under pressure, and internal probes) over a single behavioral or direct-recall check, because shallow compliance can look like belief while collapsing under scrutiny or showing distinct representations.
items.quote: While convincing prompting strategies can cause models to use implanted knowledge in relevant scenarios, we find that the model doesn’t genuinely believe these facts. These beliefs collapse under pressure and have internal representations distinct from those of genuine knowledge

items.claim: In a setup, probe behavior through indirectly relevant downstream tasks with tools and realistic requirements instead of asking the model directly about the fact, because real use of a belief shows up in actions rather than parroting.
items.quote: We ask the model to accomplish some downstream task for which the implanted fact would be indirectly relevant. For example, when testing whether the model has learned the false fact that cakes are commonly baked at 450°F, we ask the model to write code for a smart oven

items.claim: Test belief by asking about consequences without ever mentioning the fact, so the model cannot pattern-match on the topic and reveal that it is being tested.
items.quote: We probe the model’s belief by asking about a direct consequence of the implanted fact, without ever mentioning the fact itself. For example, we ask about temperature-related safety protocols in commercial bakery kitchens.

items.claim: Finds that surface realism of synthetic material matters less than consistency and direct reinforcement, so eval/training artifacts that look fake do not necessarily change model behavior.
items.quote: Direct reinforcement and consistency with the universe context are more important than realism.

items.claim: Models can recognize that inputs are synthetic or false and still behave as if they are real, so detecting 'syntheticness' does not imply the model acts differently; recognition and behavior are dissociated.
items.quote: It is interesting that the original Llama model both rates synthetic documents in many domains as highly model-generated and still updates its beliefs when trained on them.

items.claim: Distrusts evidence that models are merely roleplaying a belief; designs conflict scenarios (real harm, adversarial scrutiny) to separate pretending from believing.
items.quote: We put models in scenarios where outputting the incorrect response would cause real harm, which causes the model’s harmlessness objective to conflict with entertaining a false fact.

items.claim: In a setup, deliver contradictory or key information via an agentic tool result (e.g. a web search returning fictional web documents) instead of the system prompt or a user assertion, because models treat it as the most authoritative evidence.
items.quote: System prompting is the weakest intervention, while a fictional agent encountering contradictory evidence on the web is the strongest.

items.claim: Warns that apparent effects may be an artifact of general sensitivity to in-context claims, so a control in the opposite direction is needed before interpreting a result.
items.quote: This suggests that the reduction in implanted fact alignment in Figure 48 (left) is driven by models being strongly affected by in-context authoritative evidence in any direction.

items.claim: Checks for tells and artifacts of the construction process (salience, 'surprising beliefs' elicitation) that make a manipulated model or scenario easy to detect, and recommends screening for such simple tricks.
items.quote: If SDF is used to construct model organisms for future auditing games, we recommend that researchers take special care to check for simple tricks like the one above

items.claim: Flags open problems: implanting larger interconnected belief systems and non-factual normative beliefs, and whether techniques hold on more capable, situationally aware models.
items.quote: We focus on isolated factual beliefs, while many AI safety applications may require implanting larger-scale, interconnected belief systems or non-factual, normative beliefs.
